title: Points, lines, line segments and rays
keyIdea: A point is an exact place, named with a capital letter. A line segment joins two points and stops at both: it has two endpoints, so it has a length you can measure. A ray starts at one endpoint and goes on for ever in one direction, so it is named endpoint first: ray AB starts at A and is not the same as ray BA. A line goes on for ever both ways and has no endpoints. Only segments can be measured. Two rays that share an endpoint make an angle, and the shared point is the vertex. The sides of a flat shape are line segments.
familyTip: On a walk, play 'segment, ray or line?': a pencil or a table edge is a segment because it stops at both ends; a torch beam is a good picture of a ray because it starts at the torch and keeps going; railway tracks drawn on a map with arrows can stand for lines. Ask your child where the endpoints are each time.

visual.caption: Can a ruler measure it? Drag each figure into a box, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: join two points three ways, try to measure six figures, build named rays, open an angle between two rays and count the segments in a house.

kid: A point is an exact place. We name it with a capital letter, like A. Join point A to point B and you can make three different things.

A line segment stops at A and at B. It has two endpoints, so you can measure how long it is. A ray starts at A, goes through B and never stops. The arrow shows it keeps going. A line has an arrow at both ends. It has no endpoints at all.
When you name a ray, write the endpoint first. Ray AB starts at A. Ray BA starts at B and points the other way, so it is a different ray.

Two rays that start at the same point make an angle. That point is the vertex. Making the arms longer does not change the angle. The sides of a square or a triangle are line segments, and each side counts once.
adult: Ages 9 to 10. This is CCSS 4.G.A.1: draw points, lines, line segments, rays and angles, and find them in flat shapes. CCSS 4.MD.C.5a defines an angle as two rays that share an endpoint. In England, Year 3 and Year 4 geometry build the same ideas through right angles, turns and perpendicular and parallel lines. Key words: point, line, line segment, ray, endpoint, vertex.

A line is infinitely long in both directions, so it has no endpoints and no length. A line segment is the part of a line between two endpoints, so it has a fixed length. A ray has one endpoint and goes on for ever in one direction. Notation follows that idea: segment AB, line AB, and ray AB with the endpoint written first.

Common mistakes: calling every straight mark a 'line'; trying to measure a ray or a line; reading ray AB and ray BA as the same ray; thinking the arrow points at something; thinking longer arms make a bigger angle; and counting a shared side twice when counting the segments in a shape.

In the lab your child joins two points three ways, finds that a ruler can only measure segments, builds rays QR, QP and RP by tapping the endpoint first, opens an angle between two rays from one vertex and changes the arm length, and finds all 6 segments in a house drawing.

practice.prompt: Which figure has exactly one endpoint?
practice.hint: Count the endpoints: where does each one stop?
practice.explain: A ray starts at one endpoint and goes on for ever. A segment has two endpoints and a line has none.

practice.prompt: Points A, B and C sit on a line segment in that order. Segment AB is {a} cm and segment BC is {b} cm. How long is segment AC?
practice.hint: Segment AC is made of segment AB and segment BC joined end to end.
practice.explain: AC = AB + BC = {a} + {b} = {=a+b} cm. A segment has a length because it has two endpoints.

practice.prompt: A shape has {a} straight sides. You draw one more line segment from one corner to another corner. How many line segments are in the drawing now?
practice.hint: Each side is one segment. Then add the new one.
practice.explain: {a} sides are {a} segments, and the new one makes {=a+1}.

practice.prompt: Ray PQ and ray QP are drawn. Are they the same ray?
choices: No, they start at different points
Yes, they use the same letters
Yes, they both go through P and Q
practice.hint: The first letter is the endpoint.
practice.explain: Ray PQ starts at P and ray QP starts at Q, so they point opposite ways.

practice.prompt: Sam makes the arms of a right angle twice as long. What size is the angle now?
practice.hint: An angle is the turn between the arms, not how long they are.
practice.explain: It is still a right angle. Longer arms do not change the turn between them.

pool.prompt: Which one can you measure with a ruler?
pool.hint: Which one stops at both ends?
pool.explain: Only a segment has two endpoints, so only a segment has a length.

pool.prompt: What does the arrow at the end of a ray show?
choices: It keeps going for ever that way
pool.hint: Think about what makes a ray different from a segment.
pool.explain: The arrow means the ray never ends in that direction.

pool.prompt: Two rays start at the same point. What do they make?
pool.hint: The shared endpoint has a special name: the vertex.
pool.explain: Two rays from one endpoint make an angle, and that endpoint is the vertex.

pool.prompt: A square has sides of {a} cm. Each side is a line segment. What is the total length of all its segments?
pool.hint: A square has 4 sides, all the same length.
pool.explain: 4 segments of {a} cm make {=4*a} cm in total.

pool.prompt: Segment AC is {a} cm long. Point B is on it, and segment AB is {b} cm. How long is segment BC?
pool.hint: AB and BC together make AC.

pool.prompt: How many endpoints does a line have?
pool.hint: A line has an arrow at both ends.
pool.explain: A line goes on for ever both ways, so it has no endpoints.

pool.prompt: A triangle is drawn. How many line segments make its sides?
pool.hint: Each side is one segment, counted once.
pool.explain: A triangle has 3 sides, so 3 segments. Its 3 corners are vertices.

pool.prompt: Which name is for the ray that starts at M and goes through N?
pool.explain: Ray MN starts at M, its endpoint, and goes through N for ever.
